note: make game-check REPORTS A TRUNCATED FAILURE LIST AND READS LIKE A COMPLETE ONE. Found by The Pavement, 2026-09-01, and it made me report a wrong number to Nathan. MECHANISM: game-check-run in the Makefile is seven separate recipe lines, two of which invoke the test runner -- one against the clients/game/core manifest, one against clients/game/bin. Make aborts a recipe at the first failing line, so when core is red, THE BIN SUITE NEVER RUNS AT ALL. WHAT IT LOOKS LIKE: I ran it, read one FAILED line and five ok lines, and told Nathan the client failures had gone from five to one. That was true of the printout and false of the tree: fixing the single core failure surfaced five more in bin, four of which were pre-existing and had been invisible the whole time. THE SHAPE IS THE OBSERVING TOOL ANSWERING A NEIGHBOURING QUESTION -- the gate answers what failed before it stopped, not what fails, and nothing in the output distinguishes those. A green rc=0 IS trustworthy, because every line ran; it is only the RED case that misleads, which is the worst way round, since red is exactly when you are counting. WHAT TO DO UNTIL IT IS FIXED: after any red game-check, invoke the bin manifest test line by hand before believing the count. A real fix aggregates both, the way subfloor-run-chunked already reports all three chunks instead of stopping at the first. The same hazard class applies to any multi-line make recipe carrying more than one test invocation -- worth auditing vessel-check, world-check and atlas-check, which I have not. SEPARATE PRE-EXISTING FLAKE, NOT OURS, worth an owner before a merge: repertory_corpus::no_scene_has_fallen_below_its_recorded_floor fails under full-suite load and passes in isolation, reproduced on a stashed clean tree; one full 4919-test run of mine had it green, so it is intermittent. A flaky red in the chamber gate phase is indistinguishable from a real one.
